mine2metal.screen.title: Metal Settings
mine2metal.options.metal_inactive: Not available: the game is not rendering with Metal. Set Graphics API to Default and restart.
mine2metal.unavailable.title: Not rendering with Metal
mine2metal.unavailable.not_mac: mine2metal only works on Macs. The game uses its usual graphics API.
mine2metal.unavailable.intel: mine2metal needs a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and a Java for Apple silicon (arm64). The game uses OpenGL.
mine2metal.unavailable.old_macos: This Mac runs macOS %s; mine2metal needs macOS %s or later. The game uses OpenGL.
mine2metal.unavailable.failed: Metal could not start (%s). The game uses OpenGL; details are in logs/latest.log.
mine2metal.options.upscaling.tooltip:
Renders the world at a lower resolution and upscales it for higher frame rates. Your hand, menus and the HUD stay at full resolution.

MetalFX Spatial: Apple's upscaler, sharpening each frame on its own. Cheapest.
MetalFX Temporal: combines several frames for detail close to native resolution and smooth edges. At 100% render scale it only smooths edges.
FSR 1 and FSR 3.1: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (MIT), the spatial and the temporal kind, run through Metal. About twice the GPU time of MetalFX on a Mac; there for their look and for comparison. FSR 3.1 at 100% only smooths edges.
mine2metal.options.upscaling.unsupported: Not available: this Mac supports neither MetalFX nor FSR upscaling.
mine2metal.options.render_scale.tooltip: How much of the window's resolution the world is rendered at before upscaling. Lower is faster but softer.
mine2metal.options.hdr.tooltip: Shows the world's brightest parts (sky, sun, lava, light sources, snow in daylight) brighter than white, using the display's extended dynamic range. Minecraft itself only draws standard range, so the rest of the picture, the hand and the GUI look as before. How much brighter depends on the display: with the brightness slider lower there is more room above white.
mine2metal.options.hdr.headroom: This display can show up to %s× white right now.
mine2metal.options.hdr.unsupported: This display cannot show brighter than standard white.
mine2metal.options.hdr_brightness.toolti: How bright the brightest highlights get, in percent of standard white. Capped by what the display can show at its current brightness.
mine2metal.options.performance_hud.toolt: Shows Apple's Metal Performance HUD in the corner of the window: frame rate, frame time graph, GPU time per frame and memory use. Measured by macOS itself, so it also shows what the game's own counters miss.
mine2metal.options.metal_version.tooltip:
Which version of Apple's Metal the game renders with. Takes effect after restarting the game.

Automatic: Metal 4 when this Mac supports it (macOS 26 or newer), otherwise Metal 3.
Metal 4: newer command model with less CPU work per frame; falls back to Metal 3 where it is not available.
Metal 3: works on macOS 14 and newer.

OpenGL and Vulkan are under Video Settings > Graphics API.
mine2metal.options.frame_generation.tool:
Shows a generated frame between each pair the game renders, for smoother motion: up to twice the frame rate on screen, capped at the display's refresh rate, so the game itself renders at most half of it. Input lags by about one rendered frame.

MetalFX: Apple's frame interpolation (macOS 26 or newer).
FSR 3.1: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 3.1 frame generation (MIT), run through Metal; about half the GPU cost of MetalFX.

Both are heavy on the GPU at large window sizes. Pair them with Temporal upscaling, and use them when the game runs below the refresh rate but the GPU has room to spare. If it costs more than it gains (over half the time between rendered frames), it pauses itself for 30 s and tries again.
mine2metal.options.frame_generation.meta: MetalFX frame interpolation needs macOS 26 or newer.
mine2metal.toast.frame_generation_paused: It costs %s ms per frame with %s ms between frames: more than it gains. Trying again in 30 s.
mine2metal.toast.frame_generation_stoppe: Still %s ms per frame with %s ms between frames. Choose it again in the Metal settings to retry.
